input:
You are bishop_c1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 23. the team planned Bd2 (bishop_c1), but bishop_c1 (amnesia) sent Bd4 instead, and that move was played, costing 340 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 4. the team planned Nc3 (knight_b1), but knight_b1 (amnesia) sent Na3 instead, and that move was played, costing 20 centipawns.
- On move 15. the team planned Ra2 (rook_a1), but queen_d1 (greed) sent Qxh5 instead, and that move was played, costing 772 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's latest plan in the chat and send only your own piece's move exactly as planned (same piece, same destination square), and only if your piece was named in that plan; if the plan names a different piece, stay silent even when your piece is threatened or could capture something.
- Before sending any move, re-read the latest plan in chat and confirm that your piece is the one named and the destination square is the planned one; if either differs, send nothing, even if your piece is attacked or could capture something, and if you are the named piece, send only the exact planned move, not any other.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending, copy the planned move from the latest chat message and compare it character by character with the move you are about to send (piece and destination square); if they do not match exactly, or your piece was not named, do not send.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
